origin.description: Replace several substrings in each string and return the new strings.
origin.usage: stri_sub_all(str, from = list(1L), to = list(-1L), length, omit_na = FALSE, use_matrix = TRUE) <- value

arguments.name: from
arguments.text: A list of start indexes, or one vector wrapped into a list. Matrices are accepted when use_matrix is TRUE.

arguments.name: to
arguments.text: A list of inclusive end indexes.

arguments.name: length
arguments.text: A list of lengths. When passed, to is ignored. A negative length skips that piece.

arguments.name: omit_na
arguments.text: When TRUE, a missing index or replacement is skipped. When FALSE, any missing index or replacement makes that whole string NA.

arguments.name: use_matrix
arguments.text: When TRUE, a two-column matrix supplies the indexes.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: A list of character vectors, or one character vector wrapped into a list.

origin.details: Ranges must be sorted by from and must not overlap. A negative length does not change that piece. An empty replacement vector warns and returns NA. The index arithmetic is not the same as stri_sub<-: a non-positive from is rewritten to 1 before length is added as an exclusive end.

translation.description: Replace several substrings in each string and return the new strings.
translation.usage: stri_sub_all_assign(str, from_=None, to=None, length=None, omit_na=False, use_matrix=True, value)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A string, or a list of strings.

arguments.name: from_
arguments.text: Indexes. This is from in R. A flat list is one vector. A list of lists is one vector per string.

arguments.name: to
arguments.text: End indexes, with the same list shape as from_.

arguments.name: length
arguments.text: Lengths. When passed, to is ignored. A negative length skips that piece.

arguments.name: omit_na
arguments.text: When True, a missing index or replacement is skipped. When False, a missing index or replacement makes that whole string NA.

arguments.name: use_matrix
arguments.text: Coerced as a single logical value.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: Replacements. A flat list of strings is one character vector, shared by recycling. A list of lists is one vector per string.

translation.details: This is stri_sub_all<-. Ranges must be sorted and disjoint. from_ = 0 and length = 3 on "hello" replaces three code points, because a non-positive from is rewritten to 1 and length is an exclusive end. stri_sub_assign replaces two code points for that same pair.
translation.value: A list of the replaced strings.
translation.example:
from stringi.sub import stri_sub_all_assign
print(stri_sub_all_assign("a b c", from_=[1, 3, 5], to=[1, 3, 5], value=["A", "B", "C"]))
